title: The early-qibla convergence on Petra
statement: On Gibson's survey, the qibla walls of the earliest datable mosques point toward Petra rather than Mecca for roughly the first Islamic century, and this sits within a convergence the corpus registers — Mecca's absence from Ptolemy's Arabia, the earliest Ka'ba descriptions, the tradition's own memory of a qibla change — read alongside the canon's account of Abraham as a recruited figure of the recovery; the corpus deliberately preserves the tension between this reading and the traditional Hijaz account rather than resolving it.

includes: The survey layer at its own strength: Gibson's early-qibla orientations and the scholarly dispute over their measurement and interpretation, with the critical literature carried in full
The convergence items the Explainer assembles, each at its own grade: the Ptolemy absence, the early Ka'ba descriptions, the tradition's qibla-change memory
The canon layer: Abraham as tested, recruited figure of the recovery — the angle that makes this a Wheel reading rather than a geography dispute
The preserved tension: the corpus's Petra reading and its Hijaz-tradition material stand in deliberate, recorded tension; neither overwrites the other
excludes: Any settled relocation claim; the record registers a convergence and a dispute, not a conclusion
Polemic against Islamic tradition; the tradition's own accounts are engaged in their own voice
The canon as evidence for Gibson or Gibson as evidence for the canon; the layers are kept from laundering each other
Navigational-accuracy arguments beyond what the cited surveys actually measured

source_references.locator: 'The Truth' chapter, the Sacrifice of Abraham section (Abraham as tested, recruited figure)

alternatives.statement: Early builders lacked precise geodesy; orientation scatter reflects method, not target — the Schumm-Goldstein line, on which the Petra pattern dissolves.
The tradition's own account of the qibla change (Jerusalem to Mecca) explains the orientation memory without any second sanctuary.
The convergence assembles items of very different quality; Ptolemy's silence and late descriptions cannot carry a relocation thesis.
